result.title: The One-Pixel of Reasoning: One Truthful Relation Is Enough to Mislead LLM Agents
result.summary: Can one sentence manipulate an agent's belief by targeting a single implicit warrant linking evidence to a conclusion? In this paper, we introduce the one-relation attack (ORA), a novel cognitive attack on this inferential relation. ORA localizes a critical implicit warrant and performs a one-relation intervention using a single source-grounded sentence that qualifies this warrant and steers the agent toward an incorrect belief. Across eighteen models on biomedical inference and vulnerability detection, best-of-$10 attacks overturn initially correct answers at mean rates of 54.9% for proprietary and 80.0% for open-weight models. Attacks also transfer without victim feedback, and paired controls support the roles of targeting and qualification. Moreover, successful sentences can pass source-support checks and evade identification, and multi-agent debate raises team error from 50.0% to 59.5% in our balanced stress test. These findings establish implicit warrants as a cognitive attack surface for manipulating agents' beliefs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 one-relation attack（ORA）：定位连接证据与结论的关键隐含 warrant，用一句有来源支撑的句子做单点干预，把 agent 从原本正确的答案引向错误信念；在 18 个模型的生物医学推断与漏洞检测任务上报告了较高的翻转率、攻击可迁移性，并发现多智能体辩论反而提高了团队错误率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定位关键隐含 warrant 并作最小单点干预」的探测思路，可能为核查 LVR/VLM 推理中哪一步证据或内部状态对结论具因果作用、以及贡献分配提供可借鉴线索。
